verification.notes: Section CXV-CXVI: Vyasa's boon to Gandhari yields a mass of flesh divided into a hundred parts including Duhsasana, all born as Dhritarashtra's sons by Gandhari.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV-CXVI

verification.notes: Section CXV-CXVI: Gandhari's hundred sons, including Duhsasana, are born from the ball of flesh produced by Vyasa's boon.

note.en: Bhima kills Dushasana at Kurukshetra, drinking his blood in fulfilment of the vow he swore in the dice hall.

verification.notes: Section 83: Bhima fells Duhshasana with his mace, cuts open his breast, drinks his blood, and beheads him, fulfilling his dice-hall vow.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CXLIII (origin of Bhurisravas recounted to explain his clash with Satyaki)

verification.notes: Section CXLIII: Sanjaya narrates that Somadatta obtained Bhurisravas as a son through a divine boon.

Section CXLII: an unseen Arjuna severs the sword-arm of Bhurisravas as he is about to behead the captive Satyaki, ending Bhurisravas's ability to fight; he dies in that same encounter (referred to as slain by Section CXLIV).

note.en: Bhurishrava throws down Satyaki and is about to behead him when Arjuna severs his arm.

verification.notes: Sections CXXXIX-CXLII: Bhurisravas overpowers and throws down Satyaki in battle, about to behead him, before Arjuna intervenes.
Section 8: Ashwatthama seizes Yudhamanyu, who had struck him with a mace after finding Uttamaujas slain, throws him to the ground, and kills him during the night raid.
Section 8: Ashwatthama finds Uttamauja asleep and kills him by trampling his throat and chest before Yudhamanyu intervenes.

Section 1 of the Sauptika Parva opens with Kritavarman as one of the three Kaurava-side survivors (with Kripa and Ashwatthama) fleeing after Duryodhana's fall, fighting throughout the war on Duryodhana's side.

note.en: Kripa and Kritavarman, two of the war's three Kaurava-side survivors, rest together as Ashwatthama plans the night raid.

verification.notes: Section 1: Kripa and Kritavarman, exhausted and grief-stricken, lie down to sleep together on the bare ground after the war's end, prompting Ashwatthama's night raid.
Section 1: Kripa, Kritavarman and Ashwatthama are the three survivors gathered together at the war's end from which the night raid on the Pandava camp originates.
